home.stackLead: Most of my projects are TypeScript end to end: React and the TanStack libraries in the browser, styled with Tailwind CSS, Node.js on the server and PostgreSQL for the data. The types reach from the database to the interface, so many mistakes show up before the app even runs.
home.stackMore: At work I also build with Elixir and Phoenix and with Kotlin, and I pick up a new stack when a project needs it. Other languages and tools I have worked with:
home.workflowLead: I take a project from requirement to production myself. AI coding agents speed up every stage, while I make the decisions and own the result. I check their work with tests, type checks and CI quality gates, because I know where agents go wrong: logic that looks right but is not, made-up packages, missed edge cases. Security-sensitive parts such as authentication and data migrations I review line by line.

colophon.title: How this site is built
colophon.description: The stack, architecture, design, testing, hosting and accessibility of this portfolio.
colophon.lead: The technology and engineering practices behind this site: the stack, how pages are rendered and translated into five languages, how it is tested and deployed, and how it stays fast and accessible.
colophon.sourceCode: The source code is on GitHub.

sections.title: Stack
paragraphs: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4. The projects archive uses TanStack Table with match-sorter for fuzzy search, the contact form uses TanStack Form with a Zod schema shared by the browser and the server, and next-intl provides the language versions.

sections.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Every page is generated at build time in every language. Content lives in typed TypeScript modules, and automated checks verify slugs, images, links, dates and translations before each build.

Pages are React Server Components; JavaScript is sent only for the interactive parts, such as the navigation menus, the projects archive, the image gallery and the contact form. Each page has its own generated link preview image and structured data for search engines.

sections.title: Design
paragraphs: Colours are design tokens in CSS variables. Light and dark mode each offer several themes, applied before the first paint so the page never flashes the wrong colours.

Pages and project images move between routes with view transitions, and content rises into place as you scroll, driven by CSS. On larger screens a light particle field drawn with WebGL2 reacts to the pointer; it pauses in hidden tabs and stays off when reduced motion is requested.

sections.title: Testing and CI
paragraphs: GitHub Actions runs Biome, the TypeScript compiler, Vitest and Playwright on every push. The end-to-end tests cover navigation, search, forms and themes on desktop and mobile, and run axe accessibility checks against WCAG 2.2 AA.

Lighthouse CI keeps performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO within fixed budgets, including a limit on the JavaScript each page ships. A weekly job checks every external link, and Dependabot keeps dependencies up to date.

sections.title: Hosting and privacy
paragraphs: The site is hosted on Vercel and deployed automatically from the main branch. Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights measure visits and real loading times without cookies, and your theme choice is stored only in your browser.

sections.title: Accessibility
paragraphs: This site aims to meet WCAG 2.2 at level AA. It works with a keyboard and screen readers, keeps focus visible, respects reduced-motion settings, and every theme meets the AA contrast requirements.
If anything is difficult to use, please let me know.

colophon.assistantPrivacy: The chat assistant sends your questions, without any cookies or identifiers, to free AI model providers (Groq, Cloudflare, Google and OpenRouter), which may keep them under their own terms. The assistant itself does not store them, and Cloudflare Turnstile checks that a person is asking. The conversation stays in this browser tab until you close it. Voice input uses your browser's speech recognition, which in Chrome sends the audio to Google.

assistantPage.title: How the chat works
assistantPage.description: The AI assistant on this site: how it answers a question, which free models answer, how its answers are checked and what happens to your data.
assistantPage.lead: The "Ask about me" chat is a small AI system of its own. This page explains how it answers a question, which free models it uses, how well it scores in regular tests and what happens to your data.
steps: Your browser sends the question, the conversation so far and the page you are on to a Cloudflare Worker, together with an invisible Turnstile check against bots.
The Worker checks where the request comes from, its size and a limit of five questions a minute, then verifies the Turnstile check.
A small model picks the pages of this site the question needs, through function calling. Each question then carries a fraction of the site's text, which matters on free quotas.
The first free model that starts answering writes the answer from those pages. If a provider is busy or slow, the next one takes over within seconds.
The answer streams back as it is written, with the pages it used as sources and a few follow-up questions.
assistantPage.modelsText: Every model runs on a free tier and no account has a payment method, so the chat can never cost money. When every free quota is used up, it says it is busy instead.
assistantPage.qualityText: Every Sunday an automated evaluation asks each model the same 34 questions with known answers: facts from this site, questions in all five languages, made-up projects it must not confirm, attempts to change its rules, and a job description to compare. Fixed rules check the answers, not another model.
assistantPage.unavailable: The results are not available right now.
assistantPage.privacyText: Questions go to the model providers without cookies or identifiers, and the providers may keep them under their own terms. The Worker stores no conversations and logs only which model answered and how fast. A rating sends only the model's name and thumbs up or down. Voice input uses your browser's speech recognition, which in Chrome sends the audio to Google.
assistantPage.builtText: A Cloudflare Worker in TypeScript with Groq, Google AI Studio, OpenRouter and Cloudflare Workers AI as providers, and this site's Next.js front end. Ákos designed it and reviewed every change; AI coding agents helped write it.
